statusDefinitions.tested_case: The named test covers this individual requirement, not the whole topic.
statusDefinitions.known_missing: Gap requiring implementation and deterministic tests.
statusDefinitions.verified: Independently audited implementation and complete edge-case tests.

requirements.statement: One MP is spent per changed hexside; over-budget turns fail.

evidence.test: Facing changes cost one MP per hexside and reject over-budget or invalid turns

requirements.statement: A one-legged prone BattleMech can attempt to stand despite being unable to run.

evidence.test: A one-legged prone BattleMech may attempt to stand even though it cannot run (BMM p.45)

requirements.statement: Jumping into water uses the correct unmodified landing PSR.

evidence.test: Jump landing in water uses an unmodified PSR regardless of depth (BMM p.19)

requirements.statement: Head-aimed shots substitute the special targeting modifier for the immobile bonus.

evidence.test: Head aimed shot replaces immobile bonus with +3 (BMM p.30)

requirements.statement: Explicit ammunition-bin choices are honored when another shot uses shared ammo.

evidence.test: Automatic shared-ammo shot preserves a later explicitly reserved magazine (BMM ammo expenditure)

requirements.statement: Damage from a charge uses actual moved hexes.

evidence.test: Charge distance uses moved hexes, not shortest hex distance (BMM p.35)

requirements.statement: Physical attacks underwater deal halved damage.

evidence.test: Underwater punches, kicks and hatchet hits deal half damage rounded down (BMM pp.35,65)

requirements.statement: Head destruction is lethal to the pilot.

evidence.test: Head destruction kills the pilot rather than only disabling the unit (BMM p.44)

requirements.statement: Critical-hit transfer distinguishes the current phase from prior phases.

evidence.test: Last critical slot hit this phase does not transfer later criticals (BMM p.46)

requirements.statement: Internal ammunition explosions bypass external armor and wound the pilot.

evidence.test: Ammo explosion bypasses armor and wounds pilot twice

requirements.statement: Outside heat input is capped independently of self-generated heat.

evidence.test: External heat never exceeds 15 per turn even with repeated hits (BMM p.50)

requirements.statement: The initial involuntary reactor-shutdown PSR may succeed.

evidence.test: First involuntary reactor shutdown PSR can succeed (BMM p.52)

requirements.statement: Overheat ammunition-avoidance target numbers rise with heat.

evidence.test: Ammo explosion avoidance uses the highest heat threshold reached (BMM p.52)

requirements.statement: Each wound immediately updates and checks consciousness.

evidence.test: MechWarrior consciousness rolls increase after each wound (BMM p.58)

requirements.statement: Ammo being dumped is unavailable to fire but remains physically present.

evidence.test: Ammunition being dumped remains in the bin but cannot be fired (BMM p.58)

requirements.statement: Supported submerged weapons use rulebook underwater range brackets.

evidence.test: Underwater ranges match every supported BMM energy-weapon table row (p.65)

requirements.statement: Submerged hull damage can breach a location on a 10+ roll.

evidence.test: Underwater armor damage can breach a leg location on a roll of 10+ (BMM p.65)

requirements.statement: CASE prevents overflow transfer of internal explosion damage.

evidence.test: CASE vents an ammo explosion after RT is destroyed; pilot still suffers feedback (BMM p.47)

requirements.statement: Implement surface-dependent skid triggers and resolution.
Implement CASE II and its distinct containment behavior.
Implement AMS ammunition expenditure and interception resolution.
Implement ECM suppression and overlapping field interactions.
Implement targeting computer construction and aiming interactions.
Implement hidden-unit deployment, detection and reveal rules.
A running BattleMech turning on pavement must check Piloting before entering its next hex.

evidence.test: Successful skid PSR permits entering next hex with no fall

requirements.statement: Skid PSR modifiers follow the printed moved-hex threshold table.

evidence.test: Skid modifier table matches BMM p.68 at every breakpoint

requirements.statement: After a failed skid PSR a BattleMech slides in its previous travel direction and falls.

evidence.test: Failed skid uses prior travel direction and combined fall/slide damage

requirements.statement: Sliding distance is reduced by intervening terrain movement costs.

evidence.test: Skidding through difficult woods reduces sliding distance as specified in BMM p.68

requirements.statement: Skidding adds a +2 defensive and +1 attacking modifier for the rest of the turn.

evidence.test: Skid modifiers apply to being targeted and to shots until End Phase

requirements.statement: Skidding across the mapsheet boundary destroys the unit.

evidence.test: Skid off the mapsheet destroys the mech rather than leaving invalid coordinates

requirements.statement: Skidding into another BattleMech requires involuntary charge, avoidance and displacement.

evidence.test: Skid collision resolves fall first, then involuntary charge and target displacement (BMM p.69)
Unmoved target may avoid an involuntary skidding charge with a PSR

requirements.statement: Skidding into buildings requires building collisions and structural damage.
CASE II reduces an ammunition explosion to one structural damage point in a protected torso, venting the remainder into rear armor.

evidence.test: CASE II torso vents ammo explosion through rear armor, with only one internal hit (BMM p.119)

requirements.statement: CASE II in a limb removes up to half of its starting armor after one structural hit.

evidence.test: CASE II limb loses up to half original armor and only one structure point (BMM p.119)

requirements.statement: CASE II in a head removes half the initial head armor (rounded up) and inflicts one structural hit.

evidence.test: CASE II head loses one structure and half starting head armor (BMM p.119)

requirements.statement: Explosion-generated critical hits with CASE II are separately negated when the confirmation roll is 8 or higher.

evidence.test: CASE II suppresses explosion-generated criticals on secondary roll 8+ (BMM p.119)

requirements.statement: A confirmed CASE II critical hit below 8 is still applied.

evidence.test: CASE II explosion critical takes effect if confirmation roll is below 8

requirements.statement: CASE II is an inapplicable critical slot and leaves ordinary damage transfer untouched.

evidence.test: CASE II has inapplicable crit slots and does not prevent ordinary damage transfer

requirements.statement: Clan CASE II uses distinct 0.5-ton construction specifications and Clan technology-base restrictions.
Automatic weightless critical-slot-free standard Clan CASE protection applies to all explosive locations of a Clan BattleMech.

evidence.test: Clan BattleMechs receive automatic CASE in torso without slots or mass (TechManual p.58)
Clan automatic CASE protects arm explosions before they reach side torso
Standard Inner Sphere BattleMechs still need explicit CASE for blast containment
Clan CASE II protection takes precedence over automatic Clan CASE

requirements.statement: Resolve remaining skid path when involuntary charge misses or defender successfully evades, without illegal overlapping positions.

evidence.test: Missed skid charge crosses defender hex and applies later damage (BMM p.71)
Missed charge in the last skid hex cannot leave overlapping mechs

requirements.statement: Standard rules never trigger floating critical rerolls.

evidence.test: Floating criticals is opt-in; default location 2 stays in torso (BMM p.45)

requirements.statement: Optional initial 2 relocates damage and the TAC opportunity to the second hit location.

evidence.test: Floating critical relocates hit and TAC from initial 2 (BMM p.45)

requirements.statement: A subsequent result of 2 is an ordinary torso hit without a new TAC.

evidence.test: Floating critical second 2 loses TAC and stays side torso (BMM p.45)

requirements.statement: Partial cover rerolls floating critical location rolls that indicate a hidden leg.

evidence.test: Partial cover rerolls floating critical results for hidden legs (BMM p.45)

requirements.statement: Only regular hit location rolls trigger the optional floating critical mechanic.

evidence.test: Floating criticals does not apply to punch and kick tables

requirements.statement: The construction and MTF import pipelines must support authentic Clan BattleMech engines, equipment statistics and tech restrictions before creating Clan designs.
BattleMech left, right and forward firing arcs include all hexes exactly on their 60° and 120° boundaries, independent of floating-point rounding.

evidence.test: Firing arcs include the exact ±60° and ±120° hex-direction boundaries

requirements.statement: Successful involuntary skid charge against a defender destroyed by collision damage continues into remaining skid hexes.

evidence.test: Lethal collision damage destroys target and skid continues (BMM p.71)

requirements.statement: Damage for hexes after a skid collision resolves after that collision; the attacker must survive the initial fall before charging.

evidence.test: Missed skid charge crosses defender hex and applies later damage (BMM p.71)
Destroyed skidding attacker never resolves collision or retains pending impact

requirements.statement: Skidding terrain penalties use underlying terrain movement cost, independent of a night walking MP surcharge.

evidence.test: Skid terrain cost excludes optional night walking surcharge

requirements.statement: After successfully dodging an unintentional charge, the defender may immediately choose and resolve its full legal movement and cannot move again that phase.
An unoccupied rising hex stops a skid with frontal level-impact damage; an unoccupied drop of at least two levels ends in an accidental fall without extra skid damage for the air hex.

evidence.test: Skid into a one-level rise stops before obstacle and resolves frontal crash (BMM p.71)
Skid into higher level after one ordinary hex applies prior skid damage before impact
Two-level cliff ends skid with normal fall damage but no skid damage for air hex
Four-level cliff applies falling damage for five times normal tonnage damage (BMM p.70)

requirements.statement: When skidding into an unoccupied Depth 1+ water hex, the unit immediately stops and takes no additional skid damage for that water hex; existing submerged hull breaches are checked. (See BattleMech Manual p.70.)

evidence.test: Entering depth-1 water ends skid without counting the water hex for damage (BMM p.70)
Depth-2 water in the first skid hex stops movement after fall damage only
Entering water checks existing hull breaches after skid movement

requirements.statement: A skidding BattleMech falling by two or more levels onto another BattleMech resolves accidental fall from above, its target damage and the required displacement.
Skid interruption rules resolve compound water/building/elevation hexes and multihex building basements in correct rulebook precedence.
Each standard 2D6 roll consists of exactly two six-sided faces and their sum.

evidence.test: BMM p.7: each 2D6 roll uses two independent six-sided results and their sum

audit.notes: Manually compared with BMM p.7; test enumerates every permissible face and all relevant 1D6/2D6 combinations.

requirements.statement: An explicit 1D6 rolls exactly one six-sided die, not two.

evidence.test: BMM p.7: 1D6 uses exactly one die across all six faces

audit.notes: Manually compared with BMM p.7; test enumerates every permissible face and all relevant 1D6/2D6 combinations.

requirements.statement: A roll equal to its target number succeeds, target numbers of 2 or lower always succeed, and 13 or higher always fail with 2D6.

evidence.test: BMM p.6: equal target succeeds; target <=2 always succeeds; 13+ fails

audit.notes: Checked complete 2D6 success predicate, exact equality and automatic bounds against BMM p.6.

requirements.statement: The engine displays the actual calculated modified target number (including values below 2), while probabilities use the automatic success/failure bounds.

evidence.test: BMM p.6: ranged and physical preview preserve an un-clamped modified TN

requirements.statement: Friendly BattleMechs are illegal direct targets for ranged and physical attacks.

evidence.test: BMM p.6: a friendly BattleMech cannot be directly targeted

requirements.statement: Ordinary Inner Sphere MechWarriors default to Gunnery 4 / Piloting 5.

evidence.test: BMM p.9: ordinary IS MechWarriors start at Gunnery 4 / Piloting 5

requirements.statement: Ordinary Clan MechWarriors default to Gunnery 3 / Piloting 4, unless a pilot explicitly overrides these values.

evidence.test: BMM p.9: default Clan skill ratings are Gunnery 3 / Piloting 4

requirements.statement: Ranged attacks use the Gunnery base target number while physical attacks use Piloting.

evidence.test: BMM p.9: ranged attacks use Gunnery; physical attacks use Piloting

requirements.statement: Both sides roll 2D6; tied results are rerolled until one side obtains the higher total.

evidence.test: BMM p.10: initiative rerolls 101 consecutive ties and honors the higher 2D6

requirements.statement: The higher initiative roll wins, and the losing side acts first in the Movement Phase.

evidence.test: BMM p.10: either team can win and the losing side moves first

requirements.statement: Unequal remaining forces use the book's 2:1 and 3:1 alternating declaration batches.

evidence.test: BMM p.12: initiative batches honor 2:1 and 3:1 force ratios

requirements.statement: The turn sequence is Initiative, Movement, Weapon Attack, Physical Attack, Heat and End, without skipping unresolved selections.

evidence.test: BMM pp.10-12: normal turns advance through exactly six ordered phases

requirements.statement: A shutdown or unconscious BattleMech can consume a movement selection without changing position.

evidence.test: BMM p.10: a shutdown or unconscious unit still consumes a movement selection

requirements.statement: Support quad BattleMechs' four leg locations, mobility, facing, weapon arcs and physical attack restrictions, not just biped models.
Declare a draw when the last surviving BattleMechs on opposing sides cannot move and lack any means to damage each other, without premature termination on temporary shutdown.
Handle an unbounded series of initiative ties exactly per rulebook, or prove that a finite RNG safety cap cannot reject a legitimate valid dice sequence.
All previously declared weapon attacks resolve before any phase-induced consciousness rolls.

evidence.test: BMM p.11: all declared weapon attacks complete before phase consciousness checks

requirements.statement: After resolving all weapon attacks, the engine resolves accumulated consciousness checks before Piloting Skill Rolls.

evidence.test: BMM p.11: phase consciousness rolls occur before required piloting rolls

requirements.statement: During the Physical Attack Phase, all physical attacks resolve before checking the injured pilots' consciousness.

evidence.test: BMM p.12: physical attacks also complete before unconsciousness is checked

requirements.statement: Outside simultaneous attack resolution, wounds continue to trigger immediate consciousness checks when the relevant rule calls for them.

evidence.test: BMM p.9: injuries outside attack resolution retain immediate consciousness checks

requirements.statement: For every 2D6 result and modified target number from -3 to 15, success is inclusive and the automatic-success / automatic-failure boundaries match BMM p.6.

evidence.test: BMM p.6: all 36 dice combinations obey inclusive target checks for TN -3 through 15

audit.notes: 684 deterministic comparisons enumerate 36 possible 2D6 combinations for each of 19 representative target numbers, including impossible targets.

requirements.statement: The generic Mech abbreviation includes both biped and quad BattleMechs, while non-BattleMech types are excluded from that definition.

evidence.test: BMM p.5: the Mech abbreviation includes both biped and quad BattleMechs

audit.notes: Exact BMM glossary definition reviewed. This requirement is vocabulary/classification only, not quad combat certification.

requirements.statement: A quad declaration is never silently converted into a biped design or sold through the current biped-only MTF importer.

evidence.test: BMM p.5: quad designs never silently use biped-only construction
BMM p.5: MTF importer distinguishes unsupported quads from non-BattleMechs

requirements.statement: Quad structural topology identifies front/rear leg locations, leg-sized internal structure, six critical slots with leg actuators, and correct leg-mounted weapon/jump-jet restrictions; full quad construction and combat remain unsupported.

evidence.test: BMM p.5 and p.33: all quad limbs are legs with six-slot actuator sections
BMM p.5 quad layout is inspectable but cannot enter unsupported battles
BMM pp. 5,19: audit-only quad jump jets fit front or rear legs, not biped arms
BMM p.5 quad front legs cannot split a biped arm/torso weapon
BMM p.5: quad diagnostic record sheet shows four legs, not biped arms
BMM pp.5,45: quad front/rear leg criticals preserve their six physical slots
BMM pp.5,33: combat hit labels use quad front-leg names and distinct biped arms
BMM p.6: quad leg critical capacities and armor limits cover 20-100 tons

audit.notes: Verified only the quad chassis topology and critical-slot/actuator mapping, not quad movement or gameplay. Tests independently cover all seventeen standard masses (20–100 tons), four 6-slot legs, front/rear nomenclature, legal leg equipment, armor cap boundaries, nonexistent slot 7, critical persistence/repair, biped regression and fail-closed server admission. Underlying implementations passed all 4 GitHub Actions checks on 781ebca.

requirements.statement: Four intact legs permit lateral shifts preserving facing, at the correct terrain plus one MP cost; backward-lateral shifts obey walking-only restrictions.

evidence.test: BMM p.15: intact quad can shift into each side hex for terrain cost + 1 MP
BMM p.15: rearward quad shifts are walking-only and cannot change level
BMM p.15: destroyed quad leg disables all lateral shifts; bipeds never gain them
BMM p.15: explicit lateral order preserves Quad facing, validates all four direction names
BMM p.15: explicit lateral shift respects elevation, heavy terrain and occupancy

audit.notes: Lateral shifts available only to Quads with all four legs intact: every forward/backward side direction, surcharge 1 MP above full destination terrain and level costs, no facing change, rearward only walking and no level change, collision/occupancy and full movement budgets validated. Both shortest-path preference and explicit server-validated move orders are tested. All 4 GitHub Actions checks for implementation commit 2e93b1a succeeded.

requirements.statement: Quad standing ignores the usual Piloting Skill Roll while all legs remain intact; damaged-leg standing and two-leg attempts follow their exceptions.
Quads cannot torso-twist unless a separately enabled qualifying optional quirk explicitly grants it.
Quad front and rear leg hits interact correctly with partial cover, including Depth 1 water.
An intact prone quad without hip critical damage fires without the ordinary prone modifier and can use leg-mounted weapons.
Quad weapon location and facing produce legal forward, side, rear and leg-weapon firing arcs.
Quad targets use the rulebook's quad hit-location and physical attack location tables instead of the biped tables.
A quad with undamaged relevant hips may kick rearward with the extra +1 target number modifier and proper kick location table.
Destruction of one or more quad legs applies immediate falling, movement loss and special-rule penalties per surviving-leg count.
Quad hip critical hits alter prone fire, speed and movement status, including four hips critically hit.
A quad with no destroyed legs receives the -2 modifier to Piloting Skill Rolls made to avoid falling.
Destroyed or flooded side torso disables or removes the corresponding front leg while distinguishing the rear leg.
A quad moving sideways into a building takes collision damage from the correct impact side.
Optional quad-only torso directional mounts and torso twist quirks change the permitted arcs only when selected.
